questions.q: According to DAMA-DMBOK, what is a data owner?
options: The vendor that sells the data storage platform
Any employee who regularly uses the data in their job
The database administrator who maintains the system storing the data
The individual responsible for definition, policy, and practice decisions about data within their area of responsibility
questions.explain: DAMA-DMBOK's definition centers on approval authority and accountability within a business domain, not on who technically maintains the system.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four things a data owner is accountable for?
options: Resolving disputes when teams disagree on a definition
Writing the ETL code that moves the data
Approving who gets access to data in their domain
Setting what quality threshold is 'good enough'
questions.explain: Writing ETL code is a technical/custodial task, not an ownership accountability. Owners decide access, quality bar, and disputes, and own the outcome.

questions.q: Why does DAMA-DMBOK insist the data owner be a business role rather than an IT role?
options: It has no real effect either way — it's just a naming convention
IT staff are legally prohibited from holding governance titles
Business context about what the data actually means only sits with the business, not with whoever technically touches it
Business leaders are always better at writing SQL
questions.explain: A DBA can describe a table's structure, but only someone with business context can explain what a value actually means for the business — that's why ownership sits with the business.

questions.q: In RACI terms, which letter corresponds to the data owner's role relative to a data steward?
options: Informed (I)
Responsible (R)
Accountable (A)
Consulted (C)
questions.explain: The owner is Accountable — they own the outcome and have sign-off authority — while the steward is Responsible for the day-to-day work.

questions.q: How many accountable owners should a single data domain have?
options: Exactly one named owner
A full committee, so decisions are always consensus-based
As many as departments that touch the data
None — ownership is unnecessary once a steward is assigned
questions.explain: Shared or ambiguous ownership is a common reason governance stalls. One named owner per domain keeps 'who decides?' unambiguous.
